**Judgment Day Round 1 — PR1 issue-259-d2: code honest, but B5+RACE tests self-confirming on the load-bearing remote CAS**

**What**: Blind dual adversarial review (judgment-day, Judge A + Judge B, both opus) of PR1 of the 5-PR chain for issue-259-d2. Range origin/feature/v2.0.0..HEAD (local, unpushed, HEAD=ec41403). Focus: cursor.mjs + git-seam.mjs (foundation of PR2-PR5). Owner's 3-item brief with mandatory empirical reproduction.

**Why**: Pre-push gate. Owner ruled PR1 must clear judgment-day BEFORE push → my review → human merge → then PR2 starts (PR2 on an unmerged PR1 would anchor to a possibly-broken cursor model — the 8-commit-reset argument again).

**VERDICT: NOT APPROVED (Round 1). One confirmed blocking finding. The CODE is honest; the TESTS are not.**

**CONFIRMED (both judges, both reproduced by MUTATION):**
- B5 (cursor.test.mjs:222) and the acceptManually RACE test (cursor.test.mjs:299) are TAUTOLOGICAL w.r.t. the authoritative remote CAS. The design is remote-authoritative: the ONLY cross-runner protection is the remote `push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<from>` (cursor.mjs:77). But both tests run in a SINGLE working dir, so the second advance throws at the LOCAL `update-ref <ref> <to> <from>` (cursor.mjs:75) BEFORE the push is ever reached. Both judges mutated line 77 to a plain `push --force` (no lease) and showed B5+RACE stay GREEN, while a real two-clone cross-runner race LOSES (stale window overwrites the good cursor). Exactly the self-confirming-test class that burned the prior 8-commit slice. Judge A rated CRITICAL (test integrity), Judge B rated WARNING(real) — same finding, both reproduced. Fix (both judges agree): add a two-clone/cross-runner test where BOTH local refs are C0, one advances, the loser's stale advance is rejected ONLY by the remote lease (local update-ref must be shown to SUCCEED on the loser).

**CLEARED — owner items 1 & 2 both proven HONEST (both judges, reproduced):**
- Item 1 (automatic-path CAS hollow?): NOT hollow. `from` in advanceCursor is a pure caller-supplied parameter, never read internally. Both judges built the real two-clone race (both fetched to C0, both advancing from C0) → remote force-with-lease genuinely REJECTS the stale window, cursor stays at winner's value. The automatic CAS is genuine.
- Item 2 (tri-state ABSENT vs UNKNOWN): HONEST. Fixture-per-failure-mode (bad path, unreachable host/DNS, connection refused, auth denied, malformed URL, https blackhole): every infra failure → git exit 128 → `unknown`. Only reachable-remote-with-ref-genuinely-missing → exit 2 → `absent`. No infra failure maps to ABSENT. B3 test (cursor.test.mjs:102) + git-seam tests are discriminating.

**SUSPECT (Judge A only, but REPRODUCED with commands) — real coupled defect:**
- Human `accept` path is INOPERATIVE on a plain actions/checkout clone. `acceptManually` + CLI `accept` call advanceCursor directly whose FIRST write is the LOCAL CAS `update-ref` (cursor.mjs:75), which needs the governance ref already present locally. A plain checkout never fetches refs/governance/* (per the file's own header comment), so a LEGITIMATE accept with the correct `from`/`to` fails at line 75 before reaching the remote lease. Fails CLOSED (no wrong advance) but renders the sole human escape hatch (design §2.4) unusable on the exact checkout shape. Every accept/advance test masks this by manually running `git update-ref CURSOR_REF from` in the fixture (cursor.test.mjs:237,274,316,394). Becomes CRITICAL if PR2 wires accept on a standalone checkout.

**SUSPECT (one judge each), lower severity:**
- Judge B: advanceCursor's `from` is uncoupled from resolveWindow's base — a PR2 caller written as `advanceCursor({from: readCursor().sha, ...})` would reintroduce hollow CAS (ancestry-theater class). Loose contract = live trap for PR2. WARNING(theoretical) for PR1.
- Judge B: `to` not validated 40-hex (asymmetric with `from`'s HEX40 guard). Not exploitable (execFileSync, no shell; merge-base errors on dash-led arg). WARNING(theoretical).
- Both judges (SUGGESTION): failed remote CAS leaves LOCAL ref advanced (diverged) until next force-fetch syncCursor resets it. Self-heals; harmless in-process because it exits. Caused by the redundant local update-ref (line 75).
- Judge B (SUGGESTION): readCursor has no network timeout — blackholed origin hangs (fail-slow, not fail-wrong; git eventually → 128 → unknown; CI job timeout bounds it).

**ROOT KNOT (my synthesis, for owner ruling)**: the LOCAL `update-ref` at cursor.mjs:75 is the common cause of THREE symptoms — (1) it masks the remote CAS in every test (the confirmed blocking finding), (2) it breaks accept-on-plain-checkout (Judge A suspect), (3) it causes local/remote divergence on lease rejection (both, suggestion). Judge A's stronger fix — DROP the redundant local update-ref and rely solely on the remote --force-with-lease (proven to need no fetched local ref) — kills all three. Minimal alternative — keep line 75, just ADD the two-clone cross-runner test — closes only the confirmed finding and leaves the accept-on-plain-checkout defect live. This is a cursor-MODEL decision (foundation of PR2-PR5), so it needs owner ruling, not an auto-fix.

**Where**: brain/scripts/governance/postmerge/cursor.mjs (lines 26-40 read, 66-79 advance, 75 local CAS, 77 remote CAS, 90-100 acceptManually), cursor.test.mjs (222 B5, 299 RACE), git-seam.mjs (14-27 seam).

**Learned**: Both judges independently reproduced the same tautology by the SAME mutation (line 77 → plain --force) without collaborating — strong signal it is real. The re-slice successfully fixed the CODE (items 1 & 2 honest) but reproduced the SAME test-integrity failure mode on the new load-bearing invariant. The tests still encode the fixer's single-dir mental model instead of the attacker's two-independent-runners reality.

**Next**: STOP — asked owner to rule between minimal (test-only) vs design fix (drop local update-ref) before dispatching a fix agent. No fix applied yet. Not pushed. Re-judge both judges in parallel after any fix.
